newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates All American planned notes B minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates All American planned notes B minus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it assigned its B minus rating to All American Communications Inc.'s proposed issue of $100 million of senior subordinated notes due 2001.
The corporate credit rating is B plus, S&P said in a statement.

"The ratings reflect All American's niche position primarily as a producer and distributor of game shows, the risks of its other TV production businesses, and the company's debt burden and debt terms," S&P said in a statement.

All American's earnings mainly are derived from game shows in the U.S. and internationally, including "The Price is Right," "Let's Make a Deal," and numerous others that were acquired with Mark Goodson Productions, LLC in 1995-1996, S&P said.
A smaller contribution to earnings comes from hour-long drama and action series, such as "Baywatch," for first run syndication, it said.
"Game shows represent a stabler and lower-cost program genre than most other TV programming, affording higher operating margins and a good base of earnings," S&P said.
However, certain other series are expected to run off over time, and the company will need to replace these with new, successful shows in order to maintain its credit profile, S&P said.
All American had debt to operating cash flow of 3.9 times and operating cash flow to gross interest of about 2.8 times for the trailing 12 months ended June 30, 1996, S&P said.
